data.sourceWord: MCQ: What is the meaning of the term 'purgatory'?
data.targetWord: A state of cleansing to remove the effects of sin

examples.en-GB: Answer: A state of cleansing to remove the effects of sin | Distractors: A ceremony to celebrate the life of a dead person; A journey to a holy site; A story with a religious message

data.sourceWord: Matrimony — sacrament and covenant
data.targetWord: Marriage is a sacrament in Catholicism — a public sign of giving oneself totally to another and a covenant establishing a whole life partnership. Vows are made before God, the priest, and congregation.

examples.en-GB: AQA Q1.2 — Catholic beliefs about matrimony

data.sourceWord: Matrimony — purposes and fidelity
data.targetWord: One purpose of matrimony is the sanctification and upbringing of children. The couple promise lifelong faithfulness, to care for each other, and to accept children lovingly from God.

examples.en-GB: AQA Q1.2 — Catholic beliefs about matrimony

data.sourceWord: Genesis and stewardship
data.targetWord: The Genesis accounts of creation influence Christians to act as stewards of God's creation — caring for the environment, speaking out against global warming, and not abusing the earth's resources.

data.sourceWord: Genesis and human dignity — Imago Dei
data.targetWord: Humans are made 'in the image and likeness of God' (Imago Dei). This influences Catholics to see all people as sacred, to be co-creators, and to continue God's creative plan on earth today.

data.sourceWord: Incarnation — God becoming human
data.targetWord: The Incarnation is the belief that the eternal Son of God took on human flesh in Jesus. It shows God's love for humanity — by becoming human, Jesus could understand and share human suffering.

data.sourceWord: Incarnation — salvation made possible
data.targetWord: Through the Incarnation, God could offer salvation to humanity. Only a being both fully divine and fully human could bridge the gap created by sin and reconcile humanity with God.

data.sourceWord: Scripture: the Incarnation in John's Gospel
data.targetWord: 'The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth.' (John 1:14)

data.sourceWord: FOR: Purgatory ensures justice and purification
data.targetWord: Purgatory allows souls who die imperfectly purified to be cleansed before entering heaven. It ensures God's perfect justice while reflecting his mercy — giving all a path to eternal life.

data.sourceWord: FOR: Purgatory gives hope for the imperfect
data.targetWord: The belief that most people are not wholly good or evil but somewhere in between means purgatory offers realistic hope. Catholics can pray for the dead to help their purification, strengthening the community.

data.sourceWord: AGAINST: Many Christians reject purgatory — not in scripture
data.targetWord: Protestants reject purgatory, arguing it has no clear biblical basis and was not taught by the early Church. They hold that salvation is by faith alone (sola fide) and that the dead go directly to heaven or hell.

data.sourceWord: AGAINST: God's grace and forgiveness make purgatory unnecessary
data.targetWord: Some argue that if God truly forgives sins at confession, purgatory is theologically unnecessary. Christ's atonement is complete and sufficient — adding purgatory may imply his sacrifice was not enough.

data.sourceWord: MCQ: What is the Catholic sacramental practice of spreading the faith?
data.targetWord: Evangelism

examples.en-GB: Answer: Evangelism | Distractors: Confession; Baptism; Purgatory

data.sourceWord: Mass — the Eucharist as sacrifice
data.targetWord: The Mass is the central act of Catholic worship. Catholics believe in transubstantiation — that the bread and wine become the body and blood of Christ — re-presenting his sacrifice on the cross.

examples.en-GB: AQA Q2.2 — the importance of Mass

data.sourceWord: Mass — community and communion with God
data.targetWord: Mass brings the Catholic community together in worship, scripture reading, and receiving communion. It is a foretaste of the heavenly banquet and strengthens the body of Christ on earth.

examples.en-GB: AQA Q2.2 — the importance of Mass

data.sourceWord: Pilgrimage — Lourdes as a place of healing
data.targetWord: Catholics visit Lourdes in France, where Our Lady appeared to Bernadette in 1858. Many seek physical or spiritual healing; the Grotto and baths are central to the pilgrimage experience.

data.sourceWord: Pilgrimage — Rome and Vatican as spiritual centre
data.targetWord: Rome is a major Catholic pilgrimage destination — home to the Vatican, St Peter's Basilica, and the tombs of Saints Peter and Paul. Pilgrims seek spiritual renewal and connection with the Church's centre.

data.sourceWord: Confession — reconciliation with God
data.targetWord: The sacrament of Reconciliation (Confession) allows Catholics to confess sins to a priest, receive absolution, and be reconciled with God and the Church. The priest acts in persona Christi.

data.sourceWord: Confession — healing and spiritual growth
data.targetWord: Regular Confession helps Catholics grow spiritually by acknowledging weaknesses, receiving God's grace, and performing penance. It maintains a healthy relationship with God and the community.

data.sourceWord: Scripture: the authority to forgive sins
data.targetWord: 'Receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive anyone's sins, their sins are forgiven; if you do not forgive them, they are not forgiven.' (John 20:22-23) — the biblical basis for the sacrament of Confession.

data.sourceWord: FOR: The Eucharist is the source and summit of Catholic life
data.targetWord: The Second Vatican Council declared the Eucharist the 'source and summit of Christian life.' No other practice so directly unites Catholics with Christ's sacrifice and with each other; it is therefore the most important.

data.sourceWord: AGAINST: Prayer and sacraments are equally essential
data.targetWord: Daily prayer, Confession, and the other sacraments form an integrated Catholic spiritual life. Isolating the Mass as uniquely supreme may undervalue the role of Baptism, through which one first enters the Church.

data.answer: The Incarnation means God became human in Jesus Christ.
In transubstantiation bread and wine become the body and blood of Christ.
Purgatory is a state of cleansing to remove the effects of sin.

data.title: The Seven Sacraments of the Catholic Church
data.sourceTitle: The Seven Sacraments of the Catholic Church
data.sourcePassage: The Catholic Church teaches that there are seven sacraments — outward signs instituted by Christ to give grace. They accompany a Catholic through every stage of life. Baptism initiates a person into the Church, washing away original sin. Confirmation strengthens the baptismal grace through the gifts of the Holy Spirit. The Eucharist (Mass) is the most central sacrament — Catholics believe the bread and wine truly become the body and blood of Christ through transubstantiation. Reconciliation (Confession) restores a person's relationship with God after serious sin through the absolution of a priest. Anointing of the Sick brings comfort and healing to those who are ill or dying. Holy Orders ordains men as deacons, priests or bishops to serve the Church. Matrimony unites a man and woman in a lifelong covenant of love, open to children. Together, the sacraments form a complete system of grace covering birth, initiation, nourishment, healing, and vocation.
